Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Crime Three arrested as police intercept truck carrying 2,349 rounds of ammunition 26 November 2026 7:56pm 800 G3 rounds, 1,250 cartridges seized in Eastern Region police operation ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Eastern Regional Police Command has arrested three persons after intercepting a KIA truck carrying 2,349 rounds of ammunition at Akuse Junction.
The ammunition, comprising 800 rounds of G3 ammunition, 1,250 AAA cartridges and 299 rounds of 9mm pistol ammunition, was concealed in a green sack beneath assorted goods and alcoholic beverages.
In a statement issued on Thursday, November 26, 2026, the Police Public Affairs Unit said officers received intelligence on Wednesday, November 25, that a KIA truck suspected of carrying contraband goods from Accra towards Bimbilla was approaching the Kpong area.
Acting on the information, personnel from Operation Motherland, together with officers from the Akuse District Command, intercepted the vehicle, with registration number GS 4050-12, at Akuse Junction.
The truck was being driven by Sumaila Rashid, 32, who was accompanied by Mustapha Alhassan, 28, and Suaka Aweli, 27.
The three occupants and the vehicle were escorted to the Akuse Police Station, where officers conducted a search in their presence.
The search uncovered the ammunition concealed beneath the other goods in the truck.
Police have arrested the three suspects and placed them in custody to assist with investigations. The ammunition has been retained as exhibits, while the truck has also been impounded.
The Eastern Regional Police Command commended the officers involved in the operation for their swift and professional conduct.
"The Command assures the public of its unwavering commitment to protecting lives and property, as well as curbing the proliferation of illicit arms and ammunition in the country," the statement said.
The suspects remain in police custody as investigations continue.
